objectives.text: Given the type and application of an AC motor, DESCRIBE the operating characteristics of that motor including methods of torque production and advantages of that type.

enabling.text: DESCRIBE how a rotating magnetic field is produced in an AC motor.
DESCRIBE how torque is produced in an AC motor.
Given field speed and rotor speed, CALCULATE percent slip in an AC motor.
EXPLAIN the relationship between speed and torque in an AC induction motor.
DESCRIBE how torque is produced in a single-phase AC motor.
EXPLAIN why an AC synchronous motor does not have starting torque.
DESCRIBE how an AC synchronous motor is started.
DESCRIBE the effects of over and under-exciting an AC synchronous motor.
STATE the applications of the following types of AC motors:

passages.quote: The principle of operation for all AC motors relies on the interaction of a revolving magnetic field created in the stator by AC current, with an opposing magnetic field either induced on the rotor or provided by a separate DC current source.
Since the currents in the three windings are 120° out of phase, the magnetic fields produced will also be 120° out of phase.
by applying three-phase AC to three windings symmetrically spaced around a stator, a rotating magnetic field is generated.
the rotor cannot line up with, or lock onto, the stator field
The rotating magnetic field cuts the bars of the rotor and induces a current in them due to generator action.
The percentage difference between the speed of the rotor and the speed of the rotating magnetic field is called slip.
The rotor must, therefore, rotate at some speed less than that of the stator if relative motion is to exist between the two.
torque is directly proportional to the rotor current.
The maximum value of torque is called the breakdown torque of the motor.
The typical induction motor breakdown torque varies from 200 to 300% of full-load torque.
The induction motor is the most commonly used AC motor in industrial applications because of its simplicity, rugged construction, and relatively low manufacturing costs.
In a split-phase motor, a starting winding is utilized.
Single-phase motors are used for very small commercial applications such as household appliances and buffers.
A synchronous motor is not a self-starting motor because torque is only developed when running at synchronous speed
Synchronous motors are more often started by means of a squirrel-cage winding embedded in the face of the rotor poles.
The maximum value of torque that a motor can develop without losing synchronism is called its pull-out torque.
If we reduce field excitation, the motor will operate at a lagging power factor
Synchronous motors are used to accommodate large loads and to improve the power factor of transformers in large industrial complexes.
A VFD’s primary role is to control the speed of an AC motor by adjusting the frequency and voltage of the power supplied to it.

body.text: The rotating magnetic field cuts the bars of the rotor and induces a current in them due to generator action.
This induced current produces a magnetic field around the rotor conductors, which tries to line up with the magnetic field of the stator.

body.alt: An induction motor rotor between stator poles, with the rotating stator field and induced rotor current.

body.text: Since the stator field is rotating continuously,
If the rotor turned at the same speed as the stator field, there would be no relative motion and no induced EMF.
% Slip = (NS - NR) / NS x 100%
NS = 120 f / P
Torque depends on the strength of the interacting rotor and stator fields and the phase relationship between them.

body.alt: Graph of percent full-load torque against percent slip, rising to breakdown torque near 25 percent slip, with starting torque at 100 percent slip.

body.text: As slip increases from zero to about 10%, torque increases linearly. Torque reaches a maximum value at about 25% slip.
Starting torque is the value of torque at 100% slip and is normally 150 to 200% of full-load torque.

checks.q: How is current produced in the rotor of an AC induction motor?
o: The rotating magnetic field cuts the rotor bars and induces it
Through slip rings from the stator
checks.x: The rotating magnetic field cuts the bars of the rotor and induces a current in them due to generator action.

checks.q: An AC induction motor has a synchronous speed of 1800 rpm and a rotor speed of 1746 rpm. What is the percent slip?
During normal operation of an induction motor, what is torque directly proportional to?
checks.x: During normal operation, K, flux, and power factor are nearly constant, so torque is directly proportional to the rotor current.

body.text: The rotor is a self-contained unit with no external connections. The most commonly used type is the squirrel-cage rotor.
If two stator windings of unequal impedance are spaced 90 electrical degrees apart and connected in parallel to a single-phase source, the field produced will appear to rotate.

body.alt: A split-phase motor with main and starting windings and a centrifugal switch, beside a phasor diagram of the two winding currents.

body.text: The starting winding has a higher resistance and lower reactance than the main winding, so the current in the main winding lags the starting winding current. This phase difference provides a rotating magnetic field to produce a starting torque.
At 70 to 80% of synchronous speed, a centrifugal switch on the motor shaft opens.

checks.q: How does a split-phase motor produce a starting torque?
o: A DC field on the rotor
A phase difference between the main and starting winding currents
A squirrel-cage winding in the rotor poles
checks.x: The current in the main winding lags the starting winding current. That phase difference provides a rotating magnetic field to produce a starting torque.

checks.q: Which AC motor is the most commonly used in industrial applications?
checks.x: The induction motor is the most commonly used AC motor in industrial applications because of its simplicity, rugged construction, and relatively low manufacturing costs.
Single-phase motors are used for very small commercial applications such as household appliances and buffers.

body.text: A synchronous motor is excited by an external DC source, so it requires slip rings and brushes. Its rotor locks into step with the rotating magnetic field.
It may be started by a DC motor on a common shaft.
The motor is then started as an induction motor and brought to about 95% of synchronous speed, at which time direct current is applied.

body.alt: Rotor and stator poles aligned at no load, and with the rotor pole shifted back by the torque angle under load.

body.text: As load is applied, the rotor pole shifts backward relative to the stator pole, with no change in speed. The angle between them is the torque angle.
For a constant load, the power factor can be varied from leading to lagging by adjusting the DC field excitation.

body.alt: Phasor diagrams of terminal voltage, counter EMF, and stator current for unity, leading, and lagging power factor.

body.text: When field excitation is increased, the motor operates at a leading power factor.

checks.q: Why is a synchronous motor not self-starting?
o: Torque is only developed when running at synchronous speed
checks.x: A synchronous motor is not self-starting because torque is only developed when running at synchronous speed.

checks.q: How are synchronous motors most often started?
o: By a squirrel-cage winding in the face of the rotor poles
checks.x: Synchronous motors are more often started by means of a squirrel-cage winding embedded in the face of the rotor poles.

checks.q: At constant load, field excitation on a synchronous motor is reduced. How does the motor operate?
checks.x: If field excitation is reduced, the motor will operate at a lagging power factor.

checks.q: What are synchronous motors used for?
o: Large loads and improving power factor
checks.x: Synchronous motors are used to accommodate large loads and to improve the power factor of transformers in large industrial complexes.

examples.problem: A two pole, 60 Hz AC induction motor has a full load speed of 3554 rpm. What is the percent slip at full load?

facts.a: The maximum value of torque of an induction motor.
The maximum value of torque that a motor can develop without losing synchronism.

facts.q: Why must the rotor of an induction motor turn slower than the stator field?
facts.a: So that relative motion exists between the two.

facts.q: What makes the three stator fields of a three-phase motor 120° apart?
facts.a: The currents in the three windings are 120° out of phase.

summary.text: Three-phase voltage applied to the stator produces a magnetic field that shifts through one revolution each cycle.
Slip is the percentage difference between the speed of the rotor and the speed of the rotating magnetic field.
Torque reaches a maximum at about 25% slip. If load is increased beyond this point, the motor will stall.
A synchronous motor is not self-starting. It operates at a leading power factor when field excitation is increased, and at a lagging power factor when it is reduced.
